questions.question: A alone can finish a work in 12 days and B can finish it in 18 days. If they work together and finish it, then out of the total of Rs. 6,000, A will get:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A alone can finish a work in 12 days

B alone can finish a work in 18 days

Total amount = Rs. 6,000

**Formula used:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/12

Work done by B in 1 day = 1/18

Share of A = (Work done by A in 1 day) / (Work done by A in 1 day + Work done by B in 1 day)

**Calculation:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/12

Work done by B in 1 day = 1/18

⇒ Total work done by A and B in 1 day = 1/12 + 1/18

⇒ Total work done by A and B in 1 day = (3 + 2) / 36

⇒ Total work done by A and B in 1 day = 5/36

Share of A = (1/12) / (5/36)

⇒ Share of A = (1/12) × (36/5)

⇒ Share of A = 3/5

⇒ Amount received by A = (3/5) × 6000

⇒ Amount received by A = 3600

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: Ramesh and Suresh can complete a piece of work in 10 days and 12 days, respectively. If they are working on alternate days, starting with Ramesh, in how many days will the entire work be finished?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ramesh can complete a piece of work in 10 days

Suresh can complete a piece of work in 12 days

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = (Total Work)/(Time )

**Calculations:**

Let the total work be 60 units

⇒ Efficiency of Ramesh = 60/10 = 6 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of Suresh = 60/12 = 5 units/day

Combined Efficiency = 6 + 5 = 11 units/day

According to the question,

Work done in 2 days = 11 units

⇒ Work done in 10 days = 55 units

Remaining work = 5 units

On 11th day, Ramesh will complete remaining 5 units

Time required by Ramesh = 5/6 days

⇒ Total time required = 10 + (5/6) = 10(5/6) days

questions.question: A alone can build a house in 16 days, but B alone can build it in 12 days. A and B work on alternate days. If A works on the first day, the house will be built in how many days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A alone can build a house in 16 days

B alone can build a house in 12 days

A and B work on alternate days

A works on the first day

**Formula used:**

Work rate of A = 1/16 per day

Work rate of B = 1/12 per day

Combined work in 2 days = (Work rate of A) + (Work rate of B)

**Calculations:**

Work rate of A = 1/16

Work rate of B = 1/12

Combined work in 2 days = (1/16) + (1/12)

⇒ Combined work in 2 days = (3 + 4) / 48

⇒ Combined work in 2 days = 7/48

To find the number of days required to complete 1 unit of work:

Let x be the number of days required

Since they work on alternate days, we can calculate the work done in (2n) days and (2n+1) days:

Work done in 14 days (7 cycles) = 7 × (7/48)

⇒ Work done in 14 days = 49/48

This is slightly more than 1, hence we need to consider up to the exact day:

Work done in 13 days (6 full cycles + 1 day of A) = 6 × (7/48) + (1/16)

⇒ Work done in 13 days = 42/48 + 3/48

⇒ Work done in 13 days = 45/48

Remaining work = 1 - 45/48

⇒ Remaining work = 3/48

⇒ Remaining work = 1/16

This remaining work will be completed by A on the 14th day:

⇒ The house will be built in 13(3)/(4) days

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: Prakash can do a piece of work in 18 days. If Mukesh works twice as fast as Prakash, how long would it take to finish the work, working together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Prakash can do a piece of work in 18 days.

Mukesh works twice as fast as Prakash.

**Formula used:**

Work rate of Prakash = 1 work / 18 days

Work rate of Mukesh = 2 × (1 work / 18 days)

Total work rate when working together = Work rate of Prakash + Work rate of Mukesh

**Calculation:**

Work rate of Prakash = 1/18

Work rate of Mukesh = 2 × (1/18) = 2/18 = 1/9

Total work rate when working together = 1/18 + 1/9

⇒ Total work rate = 1/18 + 2/18

⇒ Total work rate = 3/18

⇒ Total work rate = 1/6

⇒ Time to complete the work when working together = 1 / (Total work rate)

⇒ Time = 1 / (1/6)

⇒ Time = 6 days

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: Six men can complete a work in 14 days. They started the work and after 5 days, three men left. In how many days will the work be completed by the remaining men?
questions.solution:
Formula:

M1 × D1 = M2 × D2, where

M1 and M2 = Number of men working on D1 and D2.

D1 and D2 = Days for which M1 and M2 worked respectively.

Calculations:

Let the work be completed by the remaining men in "a" days.

According to the question,

⇒ 6 × 14 = 6 × 5 + 3 × a

⇒ 84 = 30 + 3a

⇒ 84 - 30 = 3a

⇒ 54 = 3a

∴ a = 18 days.

∴ The remaining work would be completed in 18 days.

questions.question: A, B and C individually can complete a work in 12, 10 and 15 days, respectively. All three work together and after 3 days, B and C leave the work. The remaining work will be completed by A in:
questions.solution:
Given:

A, B and C individually can complete a work in 12, 10 and 15 days respectively

All three work together and after 3 days, B and C leave the work.

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency × Total Time

Calculation:

LCM (12, 10, 15) = 60

Let the total work be 60 units (∵ LCM of 12, 10, 15 = 60)

Efficiency of A = 60/12 = 5 units/day

Efficiency of B = 60/10 = 6 units/day

Efficiency of C = 60/15 = 4 units/day

Work done in 3 days by A, B, C = 3 × (5 + 6 + 4) = 45 units

Time required by A to complete the remaining work

⇒ (60 - 45)/5 = 3 days

**∴ The remaining work will be completed by A in 3 days.**

questions.question: A can complete 2/5th part of the work in 12 days and B can complete 7/8th part of the same work in 21 days. Find the number of days in which A and B together can complete the work.
questions.solution:
Given:

A can complete 2/5 work in 12 days

B can complete 7/8 work in 21 days

**Concept:**

Work efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken.

Calculation:

⇒ A's full work will take (12 / 2) × 5 = 30 days.

⇒ B's full work will take (21 / 7) × 8 = 24 days.

Total work = LCM(30, 24) = 120

Efficiency of A = 120/30 = 4

Efficiency of B = 120/24 = 5

Efficiency of A and B = 4 + 5 = 9

Days taken by A and B together to complete the work = 120/9 = 40/3 days

**Therefore, the number of days in which A and B together can complete the work is 40/3 days.**

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 24 days. A alone can do this work in 40 days. In how many days can B alone do this work?
questions.solution:

A and B can complete the same work in 24 days.

Formula used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time 

Calculation:

Let the total work be 120 units [LCM of 24, 40]

Efficiency of A and B = 120/24 = 5 units/day

Efficiency of A = 120/40 = 3 units/day

So, Efficiency of B = Eff. (A + B) - Effi. (A)

⇒ Efficiency of B = 5 - 3 = 2 unit/ day 

So, Time required to complete the work by B = Total work/ Efficiency of B

⇒ Required time = 120/2 = 60 days

∴ The required time to complete the work by B alone is 60 days.

questions.question: Raman can do a piece of work in 8 days, Sanam and Aman together can do the same work in 6 days, while Raman and Aman together can do it in 4 days. How long will Sanam alone take to do the work?

Concept used:

If A and B alone can complete a task in X and Y days respectively, then they together will take = XY/(X + Y) days to complete the work.

Calculation:

According to the concept,

(8x)/(8 + x) = 4

⇒ 4x = 32

questions.question: P₁ and P₂ can do a piece of work together in 14 days, P₂ and P₃ can do the same work together in 21 days, while P₃ and P₁ can do it together in 42 days. How much work can all the 3 together do in 12 days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P1 and P2 can do a piece of work together in 14 days.

P2 and P3 can do the same work together in 21 days.

P3 and P1 can do it together in 42 days.

**Concept Used:**

Total work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM(14, 21, 42) = 42 units

Efficiency of P1 and P2 = 42/14 = 3

Efficiency of P2 and P3 = 42/21 = 2

Efficiency of P3 and P1 = 42/42 = 1

Efficiency of P₁, P2 and P3 = (3 + 2 + 1)/3 = 3

Work done by all 3 in 12 days = 3 × 12 = 36 units

Part of work done in 12 days = 36/42 = 6/7 unit

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: P and Q together can complete a work in 21 days. Q alone can complete it in 84 days. If efficiency of Q becomes double, then in how many days approximately will P and Q together complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

P and Q can complete the work in 21 days

Q alone can complete the work in 84 days

**Formula: **

Total work = Time × Efficiency

**Solution:**

Total work = LCM(21, 84) = 84 units

⇒ Efficiency of P + Q = 84/21 = 4

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 84/84 = 1

⇒ Efficiency of P = 4 - 1 = 3

Efficiency of Q becomes double = 1 × 2 = 2

⇒ New time taken = 84/5 = 16.8 days or 17 days

**Therefore, P and Q together will complete the work in 16.8 or approximately 17 days if the efficiency of Q becomes double.**

questions.question: A can finish a work in 16 days and B can finish the same work in 15 days. After A had worked for 4 days, B also joined A to finish the remaining work. In how many days will the remaining work be finished?
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total work ÷ Time taken to complete the work individually.

**Calculation:**

Portion of work done by A in 1 day = 1over16

Portion of work done by B in 1 day = 1over15

Total work done by A in 4 days = 4over16 = 1over4

Total work remaining = 1 - 1over4 = 3over4

Total work done by A and B combinedly in 1 day = 1over16 + 1over15 = 31over240

Total time taken to finish the remaining work = {3over4}over{31over240} = 3over4 × 240over31 = 5frac{{25}}{{31}} days.

**∴ A and B would take 5frac{{25}}{{31}} days to complete the remaining work.**

Total work remaining = 240 - 60 = 180

questions.question: A man can complete a work in 15 days, and a woman can complete the same work in 25 days. In how many days will 3 men and 5 women complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A man can complete a work in 15 days.

A woman can complete the same work in 25 days.

**Concept Used:**

If M1 persons can do a work in D1 days and M2 persons can do the same work in D2 days, then the relationship between them is:

Work = M1 × D 1 = M2 × D 2

**Calculation:**

1 man can do a work in 15 days or 1 woman can do a piece of work in 25 days,

⇒ (1 m × 15) = (1 w × 25)

⇒ m = (353) w

Now, let the required work be done in ‘x’ days by 3 men and 5 women.

⇒ (1 w × 25) = (3 m + 5 w) × x

Eliminating one variable by putting the value of ‘m’ from our result,

⇒ (1 w × 25) = (3 (5 w/3) + 5 w) × x

⇒ 25w = 10w × x

⇒ x = 2.5 days

**∴ The required time to finish the work is 2.5 days.**

questions.question: S1 alone can do a work in 16 days and S2 alone can do the same work in 80 days. With help of S3, they finish the same work in 6 days. In how many days S3 alone can do the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

S1 alone can do a work in 16 days

S2 alone can do the same work in 80 days

With help of S3, they finish the same work in 6 days

**Formula used:**

Total days = Total work / Total efficiency

**Calculation:**

S1 = 16 days

S2 = 80 days

S1 + S2 + S3 = 6 days

Total work = LCM of 16, 80 & 6 = 240 units

Efficiency of S1 = 240/ 16 = 15 units

Efficiency of S2 = 240 / 80 = 3 units 

Efficiency of S1, S2, S3 = 240 / 6 = 40 units.

We have to find the Efficiency of S3,

Total Efficiency of S1, S2 = 15 + 3 = 18 units.

Efficiency of S3 = (Efficiency of S1, S2, S3) - (Efficiency of S1, S2)

⇒ Efficiency of S3 = 40 - 18 = 22 units

Total work completed by S3 (in days) = 240 / 22 = 120/ 11 days.

**∴ S3 alone can do the work in 120/ 11 days.**

questions.question: A and B alone take 4 and 6 hours, respectively, to complete a certain work. If they work alternatively each hour, starting with A first, how long will it take them to complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A's time = 4 hours

B's time = 6 hours

**Concept:**

Work and Time calculations

**Solution:**

In one hour, A completes 1/4 of the work and B completes 1/6 of the work.

Together in two hours, they complete 1/4 + 1/6 of the work.

⇒ Combined work in 2 hours = 1/4 + 1/6

⇒ Combined work in 2 hours = (6 + 4) / 24 = 10 / 24 = 5 / 12 of the work

Every two hours, they complete 5/12 of the work.

⇒ Therefore, in four hours, they will complete 2 × 5/12 = 10/12 = 5/6 of the work.

After four hours, it's A's turn and A can complete the remaining 1/6 of the work in (1/6) × 4 = 2/3 hours.

Total time = 4 + 2/3 ={{14} over 3} hours.

**∴ Total time taken is ​{{14} over 3}** **hours.**

questions.question: 5 women and 2 men can complete a work in 4 days, while 6 women and 3 men can complete the same work in 3 days. How many days will one woman and one man working together take to complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

5 women and 2 men can complete a work in 4 days, while 6 women and 3 men can complete the same work in 3 days. 

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day (Efficiency) × Total time taken

Calculation:

Let the efficiency of a man and woman be M and W respectively.

According to the question,

(5W + 2M) × 4 = (6W + 3M) × 3

⇒ 20W + 8M = 18W + 9M

⇒ 2W = M

⇒ M = 2W ....(1)

Total work = (5W + 2M) × 4

⇒ 20W + 8M

⇒ (20W + 8 × 2W) (From 1)

⇒ (20W + 16W)

⇒ 36W

Efficiency of one man and one woman = M + W

⇒ 2W + W = 3W

Now, time taken by one man and one woman to complete the task = 36W/3W

⇒ 12 days

**∴ In 12 days one woman and one man working together will take to complete the same work.**

questions.question: If A and B together can complete a work in 15 days, B and C together in 12 days and C and A together in 10 days, then in how many days can B alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together can complete a work in 15 days.

B and C together can complete a work in 12 days.

C and A together can complete a work in 10 days.

**Formula Used:**

1/A + 1/B + 1/C = 1/AB + 1/BC + 1/CA

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be W.

Work done by A and B in one day = W/15

Work done by B and C in one day = W/12

Work done by C and A in one day = W/10

Adding all three equations:

(W/15) + (W/12) + (W/10) = 2(1/A + 1/B + 1/C)

⇒ (4W + 5W + 6W) / 60 = 2(1/A + 1/B + 1/C)

⇒ 15W / 60 = 2(1/A + 1/B + 1/C)

⇒ 1/4 = 2(1/A + 1/B + 1/C)

⇒ 1/8 = 1/A + 1/B + 1/C

From the individual pairs:

1/A + 1/B = 1/15

1/B + 1/C = 1/12

1/C + 1/A = 1/10

Adding the three pairs:

2(1/A + 1/B + 1/C) = 1/15 + 1/12 + 1/10

⇒ 2(1/8) = 1/15 + 1/12 + 1/10

⇒ 1/4 = (4 + 5 + 6) / 60

⇒ 1/4 = 15/60

⇒ 1/4 = 1/4 (Verified)

Now, isolating 1/B:

1/B = (1/8) - (1/10)

⇒ 1/B = (5 - 4) / 40

⇒ 1/B = 1/40

Therefore, B alone can complete the work in 40 days.

**The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: S₁ can do a piece of work alone in 9 days, S₂ can do the same work alone in 18 days, while S₃ can do it alone in 27 days. They work together and complete the work, and receive a total of Rs. 726 as payment for doing the work. What is the combined share of S₂ and S₃, taken together from the above amount?
questions.solution:
Given:

S1 can do a piece of work alone in 9 days, S2 can do the same work alone in 18 days, while S3 can do it alone in 27 days. 

They work together and complete the work, and receive a total of Rs. 726 as payment for doing the work.

Concept used:

1. Total work = Efficiency (Work done per day) × Total time taken

2. The wage amount is already distributed among the workers according to the ratio of their work done.

Calculation:

LCM (9, 18, 27) = 54

Let the total work be 54 units.

Efficiency of S₁ = 54/9 = 6 units

Efficiency of S₂ = 54/18 = 3 units

Efficiency of S₃ = 54/27 = 2 units

So, the ratio of the efficiencies of S₁, S2 and S3 = 6 : 3 : 2

According to the concept,

Share of S₁ = 6/(6 + 3 + 2) × 726 = Rs. 396

Now, the combined share of S2 and S3 = 726 - 396 = Rs. 330

**∴ The combined share of S2 and S3 is Rs. 330.**

questions.question: Zee and Gee can complete a task together in 24 days. If the efficiencies of Zee and Gee are in the ratio 3 ∶ 8, respectively, then in how many days can Gee complete the task alone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Zee and Gee to complete a task = 24 days

Ratio of the efficiencies of Zee and Gee = 3 : 8

**Calculation:**

Let the efficiency of Zee be 3x and Gee be 8x.

Total work done by Zee and Gee = 24 × (3x + 8x)

= 24 × 11x = 264x

Time taken by Gee to complete the task = Total work / Efficiency of Gee

⇒ Time taken by Gee to complete the task = 264x / 8x

= 33 days

**Therefore, Gee can complete the task alone in 33 days.**

questions.question: A and B can complete a work in 12 days and 18 days, respectively. They worked together for 4 days after which B was replaced by C and the remaining work was completed by A and C in the next 4 days. In how many days will C alone complete one-third of the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B can complete a work in 12 days and 18 days, respectively. 

They worked together for 4 days after which B was replaced by C 

And the remaining work was completed by A and C in the next 4 days.

**Concept used:**

Efficiency = (Total work / Total time taken)

Efficiency = work done in a single day 

**Calculation:**

Let total work be 36 units ( LCM of 12 and 18)

The efficiency of A = 36 /12 = 3 units

The efficiency of B = 36 / 18 = 2 units

So A + B together do in one day 3 + 2 = 5 units

So they do in 4 days 5 × 4 = 20 units

Remaining 36 - 20 = 16 units done by A + C in 4 days 

The efficiency of A + C = 4 units

So the efficiency of C = 4 - 3 = 1unit

So, C takes 36 / 1 = 36 days to do the total work

C, 36 / 3 = 12 days to do the one-third total work

**∴ C alone completed one-third of the same work in 12 days**

The remaining work is completed by C in 8 days.

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency (Work done per day) × Total time taken 

Calculation:

LCM (25, 20, 8) = 200

Let the total work be the LCM of the time taken by different workers.

So, total work = 200 units

The efficiency of A = 200/25 = 8 units

The efficiency of B = 200/20 = 10 units

Work done by A & B together in 4 days

⇒ (8 + 10) × 4

⇒ 72 units

Remaining work = (200 - 72) = 128 units

The efficiency of C = 128/8 = 16 units

Now, C alone can complete 40% of the original work in

⇒ (200/16) × 40%

⇒ 12.5 × 40%

⇒ 5 days

**∴ C alone can complete 40% of the original work in 5 days.**

questions.question: A1 alone can complete a piece of work in 14 days, A2 alone can complete the same work in 21 days, while A3 alone can complete the same work in 28 days. The three worked together, completed the work, and received a total payment of Rs. 1,040 for doing the work. What is A2’s share in the total payment received?

Given:

A1 alone can complete a piece of work in 14 days, A2 alone can complete the same work in 21 days, and A3 alone can complete the same work in 28 days. 

The three worked together, completed the work, and received a total payment of Rs. 1,040 for doing the work.

Concept used:

1. Total work = Efficiency (Work done per day) × Total time taken

2. The wage amount is already distributed among the workers according to the ratio of their work done.

Calculation:

LCM (14, 21, 28) = 84

Let the total work be 84 units.

Efficiency of A₁ = 84/14 = 6 units

Efficiency of A₂ = 84/21 = 4 units

Efficiency of A₃ = 84/28 = 3 units

So, the ratio of work done by A₁, A₂ and A₃ = 6 : 4 : 3

Now, A2’s share in the total payment received = 4/(6 + 4 + 3) × 1040 = Rs. 320

**∴ A2’s share in the total payment received is Rs. 320.**
